summary: The "Store Manager" becomes a real Entities.EmployeeInstance recruited through the vanilla recruitment flow on the existing ba:skill_logisticsmanager skill (so it appears in My Employees, draws a wage, and is rostered by the vanilla BizMan > HQ > Schedule tab with zero patching), plus a mod-owned "plan" object that mirrors HrManagerPlan/LogisticsManagerPlanDestination: it holds the manager id, the HQ address, a skill-scaled list of supervised store addresses and a per-store limits record. The plan is persisted in GameInstance.modData, driven from GlobalEvents.onNewDay, and keeps each supervised store stocked by editing that store's real Entities.DeliveryContract. Every action produces visible feedback (UI.Notification.Notifications.Show + a permanent Entities.Contact phone thread). v1 hire/assign/limits UI is a custom ModOption.SpawnUi panel + console commands; v2 adds a Harmony-injected "Store Managers" tab on the HQ BizMan panel for the "manage it in the office" feel. A genuine new GameInstance plan type and a genuine new skill are both rejected as infeasible/fragile against the game's two serializers and unguarded SkillHelper.GetData call sites.
coreDecision: Choose B — a parallel mod-owned plan that mimics the HQ manager-plan pattern — while reusing the REAL ba:skill_logisticsmanager game skill for the manager employee. Rationale: (1) Option C (Harmony-inject a real StoreManagerPlan into GameInstance.hrManagerPlans-style lists) is infeasible cleanly — GameInstance has hard-typed List<T> plan fields, is serialized by BOTH Newtonsoft (TypeNameHandling.Auto) and OdinSerializer binary with a custom policy, and the Player.SaveSystem.CompatibilityFixes.* passes actively delete plan/employee refs they cannot resolve, so an injected type risks corrupting vanilla saves. (2) Option A (piggyback a real LogisticsManagerPlan) breaks on substance: LogisticsManagerPlan restocks a store FROM a player-owned Warehouse via DistributedWork/vehicle sim, not via DeliveryContract, needs the player to own a warehouse, and its entries live in a GameInstance list the mod cannot safely grow; the vanilla Hour==2 tick would also run it with vanilla semantics. (3) Option B keeps all mod state in mod-owned data yet still satisfies requirements 3 and 4 natively because reusing ba:skill_logisticsmanager means RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate builds the right typed subclass, EmployeeHelper.HireCandidate runs the full hire flow, an HQ desk workstation for that skill already exists, and EmployeeInstance.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift() is the ready-made scheduling gate. Fallback: if reusing ba:skill_logisticsmanager causes UX bleed (the employee also shows as an assignable candidate in the vanilla LogisticsManagers HQ tab), switch v1 to ba:skill_hrmanager (same properties, less overlap with store restocking); the deeper fallback is a registered custom storemanager:skill_manager via SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded re-injected each city load, gated behind a Harmony null-guard on SkillHelper.GetData (Phase 3).

requirementMap.requirement: 1. Everything the mod does has visible in-game feedback (notifications, phone messages, UI panels) — no silent state
requirementMap.mechanism: GAME: UI.Notification.Notifications.Show(NotificationType, headerKey, Dictionary<string,string>, secs, dupId, onClickAction, sound, track) for per-action toasts with a deep-link onClick; Entities.Contact.EnsurePermanentContact("storemanager_alerts", ContactCategoryName.Business, "employee_contact_description") + contact.SendMessage(new Entities.TextMessage(msgKey, data)) for the phone thread; TransactionInfo("storemanager:transaction_*") line items on every GameManager.ChangeMoneySafe. onClick calls InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance.fullMenu.bizMan.Open(hqAddress, tab). MOD: new Interop/Feedback.cs wraps both; Runtime/WeeklyDigest.Send extended; Runtime/DailyOperations raises a toast per restock/schedule/limit-hit event; Runtime/ManagerDirectory raises toasts on assign/detach/manager-fired. Locales/en.json + nl.json get the new keys (folder already wired via ModDiscoveryRegistry.SyncDiscoveredLocalizationPaths). UI: toasts + Contacts app thread, plus the config panel itself.
requirementMap.v1: Full: toasts for every manager action, a weekly Contact digest, finance line items, and a config panel that always reflects live plan state. onClick deep-links to the vanilla Schedule tab (our own tab does not exist until v2).
requirementMap.deferred: Custom contact icon (no ModAPI hook — falls back to the generic employee icon); prefab-perfect in-panel status bars (v1 panel is functional uGUI, not art-matched).

requirementMap.requirement: 2. You HIRE the Store Manager THROUGH THE OFFICE / HEADQUARTERS, like the HR / Logistics / Pricing Manager plan pattern
requirementMap.mechanism: GAME (v2, needs Harmony): postfix BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs to add tab id "StoreManagers" to the private _tabs list when buildingRegistration.businessTypeName == "ba:businesstype_headquarters" && RentedByPlayer; patch BizManBusiness.SetTab to instantiate/activate a mod container under the `containers` transform; patch BizManBusiness.Awake/OnEnable to build the tab menu button + container GameObjects. The candidate itself comes from the vanilla recruitment flow (Recruitment Agency dialog / Headhunters tab picking the Logistics Manager skill) or from a mod "Recruit" button calling Helpers.RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate("ba:skill_logisticsmanager", skillValue, hqAddress, demands). MOD: new UI/BizManStoreManagerTab.cs (runtime-built uGUI: plan list + add-plan + manager dropdown + supervised-store list, mirroring HrManagersPlanList/LogisticsManagerDestinationUI); new Interop/Patches/BizManBusinessPatches.cs (Harmony, 0Harmony.dll bundled in Dependencies/ per D2); new Interop/Recruiting.cs.
requirementMap.v1: Honest v1: NOT in the office. Hire/assign/configure is a custom ModOption.SpawnUi panel (Options > Mods tab, reachable in-game via pause menu) titled per-HQ, plus console commands (StoreManager.Recruit / .Assign). The panel enforces the same preconditions the vanilla HR tab does (must own an established Headquarters; manager must be an HQ-assigned, scheduled ba:skill_logisticsmanager employee).
requirementMap.deferred: The real BizMan "Store Managers" HQ tab (v2). Byte-perfect visual parity with vanilla manager tabs and reuse of the vanilla NoManagerAssignedPopUp / ReorderableList prefabs (v3, would need an AssetBundle).

requirementMap.requirement: 3. The hired manager appears in "My Employees" and behaves like any normal hired employee (same hire flow, salary)
requirementMap.mechanism: GAME: Helpers.EmployeeHelper.HireCandidate(candidate) — full vanilla hire (removes from CandidateEmployeeInstances, adds to EmployeeInstances, sets dayHired, todo, GameEvent "ba:gameevent_employeehired", app badge). Because the manager is a plain Entities.EmployeeInstance carrying ba:skill_logisticsmanager (RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate returns the LogisticsManager subclass), it is automatically a normal My Employees row paid by EmployeeHelper.PayDailyWages. MOD: Interop/Recruiting.cs (thin wrapper over GenerateCandidate + HireCandidate for the panel/console); nothing else — the mod does NOT subclass EmployeeInstance (would dangle $type in the save if uninstalled).
requirementMap.v1: Full and native. No mod-owned employee state on the employee object itself.
requirementMap.deferred: Nothing. (A custom job-title label "Store Manager" instead of "Logistics Manager" is deferred to the Phase 3 custom-skill option.)

requirementMap.requirement: 4. You SCHEDULE the manager (inroosteren) like any employee
requirementMap.mechanism: GAME: vanilla BizMan > HQ > Schedule tab. The manager needs assignedAddress == HQ and a WorkShift on an office-desk workstation whose suitableSkills contains ba:skill_logisticsmanager — that item already exists at the HQ (vanilla Logistics Managers use it). Buildings.Schedule.ScheduleAutoFiller / reg.scheduleDays[d].AddWorkShift for the supervised STORES' rosters (D5). MOD: Runtime/ManagedPlan gates all activity on Interop/GameBindings.IsScheduledAtHq(managerId) => EmployeeInstance.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift() at the HQ address, mirroring HrManagersPlanList.UpdateHrManagerDropdownForPlan's candidate filter; Runtime/ManagerDirectory reconcile also mirrors ScheduleHelper.UpdateHQPlans (unschedule => plan goes dormant).
requirementMap.v1: Full: the player rosters the manager with the vanilla tool; the plan simply will not act until the manager holds an HQ shift, and auto-detaches (dormant + notification) when the shift is removed.
requirementMap.deferred: A Harmony postfix on ScheduleHelper.UpdateHQPlans for frame-exact detach parity (Phase 3, optional — the per-tick reconcile already covers it).

requirementMap.requirement: 5. Once scheduled, you ASSIGN the manager to N stores (multi-store supervision, like GetSupervisedStores)
requirementMap.mechanism: GAME: iterate SaveGameManager.Current.BuildingRegistrations where RentedByPlayer && retail/revenue business && not already supervised by another mod plan (same shape as PricingManagerPlan.GetSupervisedStores / LogisticsManagerPlan.destinations). Cap derived from the manager's skill like HrManagerHelper.CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees / LogisticsManagerPlan.CalculateMaxDestinations. MOD: Domain/StoreManagerPlan.SupervisedStores : List<StoreAssignment>; Domain/StoreManagerPlan.MaxStores => 1 + floor(GetSkillValue("ba:skill_logisticsmanager")/25); Runtime/ManagerDirectory.AssignStore/UnassignStore enforce the cap; Runtime/DailyOperations loops the assignments each day. UI: v1 checkbox list in the SpawnUi panel + StoreManager.Assign <storeId> console; v2 the destination-list section of the BizMan tab.
requirementMap.v1: Full mechanically (assignment list + skill-scaled cap + per-day fan-out). UI is the custom panel/console, not the office tab.
requirementMap.deferred: Drag-reorder priority among stores (vanilla LogisticsManager has a ReorderableList so only the first MaxDestinations are active) — v1 just rejects assignments over the cap.

requirementMap.requirement: 6. Per assigned store you SET LIMITS (restock budget cap, staffing level, etc.)
requirementMap.mechanism: GAME: none directly — pure mod data, enforced in the mod's onNewDay logic and against GameManager.ChangeMoneySafe / DeliveryContract totals. MOD: Domain/StoreAssignment { Address Store; decimal WeeklyRestockBudgetCap; StaffingLevel Staffing; PricePolicy Pricing; ... } — this is today's Domain/StorePolicy fields moved from one global instance to one per assignment; Domain/StorePolicy kept as the per-assignment value type + the global defaults. Runtime/DailyOperations.Restock stops ordering when CurrentWeek.RestockSpend >= assignment.WeeklyRestockBudgetCap and raises a "budget cap hit" toast. UI: per-store cap slider + staffing dropdown in the SpawnUi panel (v1) / BizMan tab (v2); StoreManager.SetCap <storeId> <amount> console.
requirementMap.v1: Full: restock budget cap + staffing level per store, plus global defaults applied to new assignments.
requirementMap.deferred: Price policy actually writing retail prices (needs the PricingManagerPlan.ApplyManualPrice path — Phase 3); training budget actually driving TrainingInstance (Phase 3).

requirementMap.requirement: 7. The manager keeps assigned stores STOCKED VIA DELIVERY (manages the store's DeliveryContract) plus day-to-day
requirementMap.mechanism: GAME: SaveGameManager.Current.DeliveryContracts (List<Entities.DeliveryContract>); find/create the contract with businessAddress == store; set enabled = true, repeatingOrder = true, pick wholesaleAddress, and tune items[].DeliveryContractItem.amount so projected stock covers demand to the per-product target (algorithm copied from LogisticsManagerPlanDestination.ProcessStockTarget: target - BuildingHelper.CountTotalResourcesInStock); respect Helpers.DeliveryHelper.CanModifyContract(day); the contract itself bills the player. Day-to-day: reg.scheduleDays roster top-up via ScheduleAutoFiller, complaint handling via AI.Employees.ComplaintHelper. MOD: new Interop/DeliveryContracts.cs (contract CRUD wrapper); Runtime/DailyOperations.Restock rewritten to drive the repeating contract instead of one-off orders / ReStockingHelper shelf redistribution; on plan detach, Runtime/ManagerDirectory restores each contract to the enabled/repeatingOrder/items snapshot captured at assign time (mirrors PricingManagerPlan.originalStorePrices). Driven from GlobalEvents.onNewDay.
requirementMap.v1: Full for the delivery loop (create/adjust/disable the repeating DeliveryContract within the budget cap, restore on detach) and roster top-up + complaint handling. Runs from onNewDay.
requirementMap.deferred: Warehouse-sourced restock (vanilla LogisticsManager style) — not in scope; contract-only. Fine-grained per-product targets in the UI (v1 auto-derives targets from recent sales; explicit per-item sliders are v2/v3).

BizManBusiness.SetTab — prefix/postfix to instantiate and activate the mod's tab container under the `containers` transform when tabName == "StoreManagers", and skip the vanilla menu.Find/switch (Phase 2)

BizManBusiness.Awake (or OnEnable) — postfix to build the tab menu button under `menu` and an empty container under `containers`, both named "StoreManagers", so SetTab's name-based Find succeeds (Phase 2)

SkillHelper.GetData — postfix/finalizer null-guard returning a safe default SkillData so unguarded `.baseHourlyWage` / `.trainingCostMultiplier` / `.secondarySkill` / `.icon28` / `.associatedColorGradient` call sites do not NPE (Phase 3 — ONLY if adopting a registered custom storemanager:skill_manager; not needed while reusing ba:skill_logisticsmanager)

ScheduleHelper.UpdateHQPlans — postfix to mark the mod plan dormant when the manager loses their last HQ WorkShift, for frame-exact parity with vanilla manager plans (Phase 3, optional — per-tick reconcile already covers this)
assetBundleNeeded: Phase 1 + Phase 2: NONE — the config panel (ModOption.SpawnUi) and the v2 BizMan tab are built at runtime with uGUI/TextMeshPro parented under existing game canvases (AssetService.RemapShaders not needed for code-built UI).

Phase 3 (optional, for prefab-perfect native look): a "StoreManagerTab" uGUI prefab (plan list + detail panel styled to match the vanilla HR/Logistics manager tabs) shipped via IModBigAmbitions.RelativeAssetBundlePaths + AssetService.Spawn + RemapShaders.

Phase 3 (optional, only if adopting a custom skill): a SkillData .asset + 28px icon Sprite + associatedColorGradient, authored in a Unity project on the game's exact Unity version, loaded from a mod bundle and handed to SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded.
persistence: Primary sink: GameInstance.modData (public Dictionary<string,string> on the save root, confirmed unused by the base game, round-trips both the Newtonsoft TypeNameHandling.Auto path and the OdinSerializer binary path). Key \"StoreManager.plans.v1\" -> an OdinSerializer JSON blob of List<Domain.StoreManagerPlan>. Each plan is keyed by the manager's Entities.EmployeeInstance.id plus the HQ Address string, and carries: ManagerEmployeeId, HqAddress, List<StoreAssignment> (each with the store Address, WeeklyRestockBudgetCap, StaffingLevel, PricePolicy, and a captured pre-manager DeliveryContract snapshot for restore-on-detach), WeekTally accumulators, MistakeSeed, and a Dormant flag + grace-day counter. Write on GlobalEvents.onSaveGame (fires before serialize in SaveGameManager.Save); read on [ModEntryOnCityLoad] from SaveGameManager.Current.modData. Interop/Serialization.cs keeps using OdinSerializer; only the sink moves from the persistentDataPath file to modData. Fallback sink: Interop/ModDataStore.cs JSON file under Application.persistentDataPath/Mods/StoreManager, keyed by save identity — used only if a modData read returns empty on a save the mod believes had a plan (guards against an Odin binary round-trip failure on a large string; flagged as an open question). Reload survival: on city load, each plan is revived only if EmployeeHelper.GetEmployeeById(ManagerEmployeeId) resolves; unresolved plans are dropped and their DeliveryContract snapshots restored. In-game firing sync: subscribe GlobalEvents.onJobChange AND reconcile every onNewDay — if the manager employee is gone (fired/quit/poached) or !IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift() at the HQ, set Dormant, fire a toast + phone message, hold the record for a 3-day grace window (in case of re-hire/re-schedule), then delete it and restore every supervised store's DeliveryContract to its captured snapshot. OnUnloadAsync flushes then clears in-memory state so an uninstall is clean (the modData entry is left in place, harmless, and re-adopted if the mod is reinstalled).
decisionAmendments: D3: 'A hired manager is a data role attached to a business/building; no character model' -> 'The manager is a real Entities.EmployeeInstance recruited through the vanilla recruitment flow on ba:skill_logisticsmanager, hired via EmployeeHelper.HireCandidate, appearing in My Employees with a real wage and a player-set schedule. The mod adds only the supervision plan on top and never subclasses EmployeeInstance. Still no bespoke NPC body / pathfinding / floor presence.'

D4: 'Digest -> smartphone messages; policy knobs -> a global ModOptions panel; a bespoke native window is deferred; open question whether ModOptions can be per-store' -> 'Weekly digest via Entities.Contact/TextMessage AND a per-action UI.Notification.Notifications.Show toast with a deep-link onClick. Hire/assign/per-store-limits UI ships in v1 as a custom ModOption.SpawnUi panel that IS per-store (not global-only); global ModOptions keeps only default values for new assignments. v2 adds a Harmony-injected "Store Managers" tab on the HQ BizMan panel.'

D5: add 'The manager is rostered by the player through the vanilla BizMan > HQ > Schedule tab. The mod plan is gated on EmployeeInstance.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift() at the HQ (mirrors HrManagersPlanList's candidate filter) and goes dormant when the manager is unscheduled (mirrors ScheduleHelper.UpdateHQPlans). ScheduleAutoFiller is still used for the SUPERVISED STORES rosters, not the manager.'

D6: 'Persist a per-store StoreManagerData record keyed by mod id + store id, written into the game save' + Phase-0 revision 'JSON file under persistentDataPath keyed by save name' -> 'Persist a plan-centric List<StoreManagerPlan> (keyed by manager EmployeeInstance.id + HQ Address) into GameInstance.modData["StoreManager.plans.v1"], flushed on GlobalEvents.onSaveGame, loaded on [ModEntryOnCityLoad]. The persistentDataPath JSON file is demoted to a fallback sink. Live-fire sync via GlobalEvents.onJobChange + per-tick reconcile against EmployeeHelper.GetEmployeeById, with a 3-day grace window and DeliveryContract restore-on-detach.'

D7: unchanged — no departments / Team Leaders in v1 or v2. (Note: because a mod plan has exactly ONE manager like every vanilla HQ plan, the Domain/ManagerRank ladder collapses to a single Manager role in v1.)
D2: unchanged in intent, now definitely exercised in Phase 2 — bundled 0Harmony.dll in Dependencies/, patch targets are BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs / SetTab / Awake. Phase 1 ships with zero Harmony.

NEW D9 (core architecture): Build a parallel mod-owned plan (Option B) that mimics HrManagerPlan/LogisticsManagerPlanDestination, reusing the real ba:skill_logisticsmanager skill for the manager employee. Reject Option A (piggyback a real LogisticsManagerPlan — wrong restock source, un-growable GameInstance list) and Option C (Harmony-inject a real plan type into GameInstance — infeasible against Newtonsoft + OdinSerializer + CompatibilityFixes purge passes). Fallback: ba:skill_hrmanager if the logistics-skill UX bleed is bad.

NEW D10 (manager skill): v1 reuses ba:skill_logisticsmanager (zero NPE risk; native subclass, wage curve, HQ desk, scheduler all work). A registered custom storemanager:skill_manager via SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded (re-injected every city load) is a Phase 3 option, contingent on verifying the ~8 unguarded SkillHelper.GetData(name).<field> call sites in a running game, with a Harmony null-guard on SkillHelper.GetData as the safety net.

phases.riskyItem: Runtime/DailyOperations.Restock driving Entities.DeliveryContract from an onNewDay handler: unverified whether DeliveryHelper.CanModifyContract's window is open at that point in the tick, whether creating a contract from scratch (choosing wholesaleAddress) is safe, and whether the mod's edits survive the game's own BusinessHelper.HandleWholesaleDeliveries pass on the same day. Mitigate by testing against an existing player contract first and only creating new ones once the edit path is confirmed.

phases.riskyItem: The Harmony patches on BizManBusiness (SetUpTabs/SetTab/Awake): the tab list is a private List<string>, tabs are name-matched prefab children of a serialized `containers` transform, and this UI is the most likely thing to change between Big Ambitions builds. A bad patch could break the entire HQ panel. Mitigate with defensive try/catch, a DegradedToPanel fallback to the ModOption.SpawnUi UI, and a game-version check logged at load.

Odin serialization policy skips [Obsolete] members — ensure no StoreManagerPlan/StoreAssignment field is ever marked obsolete during refactors or it silently stops persisting.
Multi-store fan-out cost accounting: per-store budget caps must be tracked independently in WeekTally or one busy store can starve the others' restock.
